- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish correction.  
- Model frequently over-estimates price peaks in the short term (1–3 days after spike) — apply downward adjustment of 2–5% for immediate post-spike periods.  
- Model under-estimates mean reversion in medium-term (5–15 day horizon) — add 1–3% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.67), model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of true trend.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently under-estimates final 5–7 days — apply 1–3% upward correction for last 7 days of forecast.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) over 3+ days, model over-optimistically forecasts upward — reduce forecast by 1–2% to reflect subdued sentiment.
